Subject: Production: sudden p99 latency and 500s on our on‑prem cluster

Neha —

We're seeing a large regression starting ~10:45am PDT across our on‑prem deployment (cluster: med-sync-prod‑us‑1). P99 latency jumped from ~180ms to +2.3s and we're seeing a large number of 500/502s. This started shortly after we applied the inference runtime config update you recommended last week (disable_dynamic_kv_eviction=true).

We've attached an initial set of logs and sample traces. Can your team triage? This is impacting customer-facing features and our ops team is getting escalations.

Attachments: diagnostics_20270502.tar.gz (120MB log archive)

— Elena

Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency and 500s on our on‑prem cluster

Quick triage update (initial findings):

What we see:
- Traffic pattern: sustained increase in concurrent small‑prompt requests between 10:40–11:00 (burst from a scheduled nightly job change).
- Error type: majority 5xx tracebacks are DecoderTimeout and KVCACHE_MISS handling slow paths.
- Cluster: nodes reporting elevated GPU decode stalls and slow remote metadata lookups.

Hypothesis:
- The recent config change (disable_dynamic_kv_eviction=true) caused larger KV cache retention, increasing memory churn and triggering slower fallback code paths for cache misses under bursty small‑prompt patterns. The decoder is experiencing longer stalls under these conditions and timeouts are cascading into 502s/503s.

Immediate mitigations (we can apply within 30–45m):
1) Temp revert the config to enable dynamic KV eviction (roll back the change) — expected impact: restore baseline p99 within 10–20m of rolling restart of serving processes.
2) Increase decoder timeout thresholds + bump batch window to safely absorb the burst (config patch).
3) If rollback not acceptable in your maintenance window, we can deploy a targeted hotfix that forces softer eviction and increases local memory buffer pools (lower risk than full rollback).

I've attached a one‑page diagnostics summary and opened OPS‑4521 with traces. If we get approval I'll schedule the rollback now and coordinate a 2‑node rolling restart pattern to keep throughput.

Attachments: remediation_plan_20270502.pdf

— Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency and 500s on our on‑prem cluster

Elena —

Thanks for reporting. We can move fast on this. Proposed short plan (need your sign‑off):
- Option A (preferred): Immediate rollback to prior KV eviction behavior. Roll 2 nodes at a time, monitor p99 and error rate. Estimated total time: 45–60 minutes.
- Option B (if rollback conflicts with your change freeze): Apply the hotfix that softens eviction and raises decoder timeouts. Estimated total time: 60–90 minutes.

Mutual action items:
- Medisync: confirm approval for Option A or B and any blackout windows.
- Redwood: will provide runbook + on‑call lead in the war room and keep a single Slack channel for updates.

Proposed war‑room: 12:45pm PDT (today). If that works we will start the rollback prep immediately and hold the first rolling restart at 12:50pm.

— Marissa Cole

Thanks, team. We approve Option A (rollback).

Two notes:
1) We have a maintenance freeze after 18:00 PDT, so please complete the remediation and confirm stability before then.
2) If we don't have a working environment by 18:00 PDT we'll need to open a formal incident report for downstream SLA assessment — please include any credits or remediation allowances in your post‑mortem.

I'll join the 12:45 war‑room.

— Elena
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 02 May 2027 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden p99 latency and 500s on our on‑prem cluster — rollback completed

Team —

Update from the war‑room: we executed Option A (rollback of disable_dynamic_kv_eviction) with a 2‑node rolling restart pattern starting 12:52pm. By 13:10pm PDT p99 returned to baseline (~190ms) and 5xx rate dropped to normal. We ran extended soak until 17:40 and verified no regression on heavy small‑prompt workloads.

What we delivered:
- Rolled back the KV eviction change across med‑sync‑prod‑us‑1 (2 nodes at a time).
- Increased soft decoder timeout by 15% as a precautionary buffer (non‑breaking).
- Opened OPS‑4521 with full traces and remediation notes.

Next steps (for post‑mortem and follow‑up):
- Joint post‑mortem to be scheduled tomorrow — we'll include timeline, root cause analysis, and recommended safe tuning profile for on‑prem (recommended: moderate KV retention + decoded buffer pool + throttling for small prompt bursts).
- Laura to sign off on a stable config that we can ship as a safe default for Medisync.
- We'll provide an operations runbook patch that your on‑call team can apply for similar incidents.

Elena — thank you for the quick sign‑off and for the log bundle; that made triage much faster. If you want, we can also prepare a short impact summary for your leadership that includes the remediation actions and recommended configuration baseline.

Attachments: remediation_plan_20270502.pdf, diagnostics_20270502.tar.gz
Jira: https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/OPS-4521

— Neha Kapoor
